newsitem.title: USA: San Onofre inspection uncovers some tube erosion.
newsitem.headline: San Onofre inspection uncovers some tube erosion.

text.p: An inspection at the San Onofre nuclear power plant's Unit 3, located near San Clemente in southern California, has turned up some erosion in heat transfer tubing but the deterioration is limited.

In a statement issued late Friday by Southern California Edison, the electric utility said the small tubes, numbering about 9,000 each in two of the unit's steam generators, transfer heat from the reactor coolant to water.
"The areas affected appear limited in extent, and inspections done to date indicate that most areas are unaffected," the electric utility said.
Unit 3 is currently undergoing a scheduled refueling outage that is set to conclude on June 26.

The cause of the erosion is still being investigated, but preliminary analysis indicates the deterioration resulted from changes in flow patterns caused by a thin coating of deposits, which can be removed during the outage.
Corrective actions may include removing some tubes from service by plugging, which is a routine response to a variety of steam generator problems, the utility said.
Results of additional inspections and analyses, which should be completed by the end of May, will be reviewed with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in early June.
An inspection of steam generators at San Onofre's Unit 2 was recently completed, and the similar tube supports showed no signs of the erosion described above.

The San Onofre plant is 75 percent owned by Southern California Edison, the principal operating unit of Edison International, 20 percent owned by Enova Corp and the remainder is owned by local municipalities.
